data.title: Punch biopsy
data.summary: Full-thickness skin sample with a circular punch for histopathology or DIF
data.body:
A punch biopsy gives a full-thickness cylinder of epidermis, dermis and upper fat. It is the standard biopsy for inflammatory dermatoses and many tumours. Choosing the right lesion and site, and handling the specimen gently, matters more than the technique itself.

## Indications
- Inflammatory dermatoses where histology helps (lichenoid, psoriasiform, granulomatous, vasculitis)
- Immunobullous disease: lesional biopsy for H&E, perilesional biopsy for direct immunofluorescence (DIF)
- Suspected tumours where an incisional sample is enough (small BCC, CTCL, granulomas)
- Hansen's disease and other infections (with tissue for culture)
- Hair disorders (4 mm scalp biopsies for horizontal and vertical sections)

## Contraindications
- Infection at the site
- Uncontrolled bleeding diathesis (relative; do not stop warfarin or antiplatelets for a punch biopsy, check INR if very high)
- Allergy to local anaesthetic (use alternative agent or saline)
- Lesions where full excision is needed (suspected melanoma: excision biopsy preferred)
- Caution: shins in elderly or diabetic patients, over nerves (lateral neck, ulnar groove, temple)

## Pre-procedure
- Consent: small scar, bleeding, infection, hypertrophic scar or keloid (ask about history), pigment change
- Choose a new, fully developed, untreated lesion; avoid excoriated, crusted or ulcerated areas
- Blister: lesional for H&E at edge of a fresh blister; DIF from perilesional skin within 1 cm
- Label the site on a diagram; photograph
- Request form with history and differential diagnoses

## Equipment
- Sterile punch 3–4 mm (6 mm for panniculitis or alopecia, 2 mm for face)
- Lignocaine 2% (with adrenaline unless contraindicated), 26–30G needle
- Fine-toothed forceps or skin hook, iris scissors, needle holder
- Suture: 4-0 nylon/silk (body), 5-0 or 6-0 (face)
- Formalin 10% (volume 10–20 times the specimen) and Michel's medium or saline for DIF

## Procedure step by step
1. Clean with povidone-iodine or chlorhexidine; drape.
2. Infiltrate local anaesthetic intradermally around and under the site (lignocaine maximum ~4.5 mg/kg plain, ~7 mg/kg with adrenaline).
3. Stretch the skin perpendicular to the relaxed skin tension lines so the wound becomes an ellipse.
4. Hold the punch vertical and rotate with gentle downward pressure until you feel a give at the subcutaneous fat.
5. Lift the core with a needle or forceps holding only the fat; avoid crushing the epidermis.
6. Cut the base at the level of fat with scissors.
7. Place immediately in formalin (or Michel's/saline for DIF). Label clearly.
8. Achieve haemostasis with pressure; close with one or two simple interrupted sutures (3 mm may heal by secondary intention).
9. Apply antibiotic ointment and a dressing.

## Post-procedure care
- Keep dry for 24–48 h; then clean daily with water and apply ointment
- Suture removal: face 5–7 days; trunk and arms 10–14 days; legs and back 14 days
- Report fever, spreading redness or pus

## Complications & management
- Bleeding: firm pressure for 10 minutes; additional suture
- Infection: topical or oral antibiotic
- Hypertrophic scar or keloid: intralesional steroid
- Non-diagnostic sample: discuss with the pathologist; rebiopsy with better site choice

## Sessions & follow-up
- Single procedure; review at suture removal
- Follow up the histopathology report and correlate clinically
